name: Battle of Legnano
summary: At the Battle of Legnano (May 29, 1176), the Lombard League, a coalition of northern Italian city communes, defeats Holy Roman Emperor Frederick Barbarossa's army. The key factor: the Lombard infantry militia, fighting from behind the carroccio (a sacred battle wagon with a bell and standard), used spear formations that halted Barbarossa's cavalry charge. Barbarossa's horse was killed; he fled the battlefield, which his forces interpreted as his death, causing a rout. The battle forces Barbarossa to negotiate the Peace of Constance (1183), recognizing communal self-governance.

_quarry.structural_significance: First great infantry victory over feudal cavalry; establishes the political independence of northern Italian communes; Peace of Constance formally recognizes communal autonomy; models infantry tactics that later armies adopt
